evidence: WindowsHelloVerificationProvider uses Windows.Security.Credentials.UI.UserConsentVerifier and the desktop-only IUserConsentVerifierInterop::RequestVerificationForWindowAsync operation bound to a native HWND.

The OS call receives only a fixed Research Observatory message and returns a typed enum. No PIN, face, fingerprint, biometric template, password, username, domain, token, or credential buffer enters the Hello adapter.

VerificationAvailability and the strict versioned VerificationAvailabilitySnapshot expose checking, available, not-present, not-configured, policy-disabled, busy, unavailable, and failed; VerificationOutcome retains succeeded, cancelled, denied, unavailable, busy, and failed.

DeviceNotPresent, NotConfiguredForUser, DisabledByPolicy, DeviceBusy, RetriesExhausted, Canceled, Verified, unknown values, activation errors, and operation errors are exhaustively and deterministically mapped and contract-tested.

The provider prechecks availability and does not request verification for not-present, not-configured, policy-disabled, unsupported, busy, failed, or zero-window conditions. Only Verified maps to Succeeded.

The Hello module has no reference to CredUIPromptForCredentialsW, LogonUserW, WindowsPasswordVerificationProvider, or password buffers. All adverse outcomes enter the existing manager's locked-only path, and no automatic password or no-login fallback exists.

application_lock_password_recovery is a separate argument-free native command and is never invoked by the Hello provider or primary unlock command. Its invocation is the deliberate recovery selection boundary.

Recovery delegates to the unchanged WindowsPasswordVerificationProvider path, which still requires LogonUserW success plus EqualSid between the returned token and desktop process token; only native success emits an unlocked event.
The non-Windows implementation returns unavailable and its cfg-gated regression test prohibits fabricated success; unavailable desktop interop activation also maps to unavailable.

The release-authoritative Windows x64 library and example harness compiled and ran. This host truthfully returned not-present, so no interactive success was claimed; injectable OS boundaries prove the configured Verified path while every deterministic denial/cancellation/unavailable/restart boundary remains enforced.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: W1.A05.T02 changes an authentication/provider boundary, adds a desktop WinRT dependency surface, publishes a versioned native/renderer availability contract, and exposes a separate password-recovery command. Credible failures are using the UWP CoreWindow method instead of the HWND interop, treating an unavailable or unknown OS state as success, silently falling back to password, allowing a missing/stale window, receiving or retaining credential material, replaying a successful prompt after a lock-generation change, weakening same-SID password recovery, malformed cross-process state, or changing existing password/restart behavior. The selected native mapping and manager tests, live Windows availability harness, strict renderer decoder tests, source-boundary checks, broad password security replay, locked dependency resolution, Rust/TypeScript/Python quality checks, architecture validation, and Git hygiene cover those risks. The current host reports not-present, so an actual interactive Verified result is conditional hardware/user-presence coverage rather than a fabricated task claim.
